md_name: Herbicide candidate characterization and bioactivity workflow
md_description: This workflow follows synthesized herbicide candidate compounds from laboratory production through purification, molecular characterization by NMR and mass spectrometry, and in vitro bioactivity assessment against plant enzymes and cellular pathways. It produces analytical signals and derived summaries used to evaluate molecular identity, physicochemical properties, potency, selectivity, and potential toxicity for agricultural application.

herbicide_candidate_batch.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic identity and origin/provenance fields for the herbicide candidate batch. I excluded synthesis protocol details, purification conditions, analytical instrument settings, raw file properties, and computed characterization/bioactivity results because those belong to downstream Process, Capture, Signal, and Derivative nodes respectively. I also avoided sample/experiment identifiers if they might be repeated elsewhere, but a batch-level identifier is appropriate here as the root entity identity for this material. Because no fields were already_generated were provided, there was no overlap constraint to resolve beyond staying within entity territory.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for this herbicide candidate batch, assigned at the point the synthesized material is first registered in the workflow; use a stable string such as HB-2026-001. This identifies the batch across purification and characterization steps.
Number of distinct herbicide candidate compounds present in the batch at registration, counted before purification and characterization; typical range 1-100+ depending on library size.
Source of the starting material for this batch at the time it enters the workflow; indicates whether the material was synthesized in-house or obtained from another source.
Date the batch was synthesized or first isolated as crude candidate material, recorded at batch creation; format YYYY-MM-DD.
Physical state/condition of the batch upon entry to purification, describing the intrinsic material quality before any downstream processing; assess as a simple categorical status.

compound_synthesis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only synthesis-operation metadata: how the laboratory transformation was performed, key reagents/precursors, major reaction settings, and a process-level outcome/quality indicator. I excluded intrinsic properties of the starting batch, purification details, and any downstream analytical or assay results because those belong to Entity, downstream Process, or Capture/Signal/Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there was no duplication constraint beyond staying within the synthesis-process territory.

md_schema.descr: Primary precursor materials used as inputs for the synthesis step, recorded at reaction setup; provide a concise string listing the starting materials or their internal names, e.g. 'aniline derivative + acyl chloride'.
Type of synthetic transformation performed during compound synthesis, recorded at the time the reaction is initiated; use a controlled category describing the main chemistry class.
Setpoint temperature in degrees Celsius used during the synthesis reaction, measured/controlled while the reaction is running; typical range -20 to 150 °C.
Total elapsed reaction time in minutes from reagent mixing to quench/workup initiation; recorded at process completion, typically 5 to 2880 minutes.
Main solvent or solvent system used for the synthesis step, recorded at reaction setup; provide the solvent name or mixture description, e.g. 'DCM' or 'THF:water'.

Key catalyst, base, ligand, or other enabling reagent used to drive the synthesis, recorded at setup; provide a concise string including the reagent name and, if relevant, loading such as 'Pd(PPh3)4, 5 mol%'.
Isolated or estimated yield of crude herbicide candidate material from the synthesis step, measured at process end; typical range 0-100%.
Overall process outcome for the synthesis step, recorded after workup or crude isolation, indicating whether crude candidate material was successfully produced.

purified_compound_library.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the purified compound library: what it is, its composition, and its provenance after purification. I excluded synthesis reaction settings, analytical capture settings, raw signal file properties, and derived characterization/bioactivity results because those belong to upstream Process nodes, downstream Capture nodes, Signal nodes, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided reusing any possible sample identifiers that would ordinarily belong to the original batch/entity unless needed for lineage; instead I focused on purification-stage identity and composition appropriate for the purified material itself.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified compound library, assigned when purified material is registered for characterization and bioactivity testing; use a stable string such as PCL-001.

Identifier of the upstream crude herbicide candidate batch from which this purified library was prepared, recorded at library registration; use the same batch-style string format as the originating entity.
Number of distinct purified compounds included in the library at the time it is prepared for downstream measurements; typical range 1-100+.
Overall purification state of the library at the point it enters characterization, indicating how completely impurities were removed relative to the intended workflow standard.
Estimated purity of the purified compound library as a percentage at release for characterization/testing; measured after purification and before downstream capture, typical range 0-100%.

Immediate storage condition used for the purified library before NMR, MS, or bioassay preparation, recorded at library handoff; include temperature or medium in a concise string such as '-20 C, desiccated' or 'DMSO stock'.

nmr_spectroscopy.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration metadata for the NMR acquisition: hardware identity, nucleus/probe configuration, acquisition mode, and actively controlled settings that define how the spectrum was recorded. I excluded sample identity and purification-state fields because they belong to the upstream Entity node, and I excluded raw file properties or spectral outputs because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided analytical interpretation or structure calls, since those are captured by the separate Process node that interprets the NMR spectrum. No already_generated fields were provided here, so there was no duplication constraint beyond staying in capture territory.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the NMR spectrometer used for this capture session, recorded at acquisition setup; e.g. 'Bruker' or 'JEOL'.
Model name or number of the NMR spectrometer used for the measurement session, recorded at acquisition setup; e.g. 'Avance Neo 600'.
Serial number of the NMR spectrometer used for the capture session, recorded to identify the exact instrument configuration; use the manufacturer-assigned serial string.
Nucleus observed during NMR acquisition, recorded at the start of the measurement session; typically one of the common observed nuclei used for structural confirmation.
Operating frequency of the NMR spectrometer in MHz for the observed nucleus, recorded at acquisition setup; typical range 60-1200 MHz.
Type of NMR probe installed for the capture session, recorded at acquisition setup; indicates the hardware configuration used to acquire spectra.

Data acquisition mode used for the NMR session, recorded while configuring the instrument; describes whether the measurement was a 1D or multidimensional experiment and the general acquisition strategy.
Number of transients collected for the NMR measurement, set before acquisition begins; typical range 1-10000 and used to control signal-to-noise.
Name of the NMR pulse sequence used during capture, recorded at acquisition setup; provide the exact sequence label or a clear standard name such as 'zg30'.
Sample temperature during the NMR measurement session, controlled by the spectrometer at acquisition time; typical range -100 to 150 °C.

nmr_spectrum.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw-data artefact properties of the NMR spectrum: file identity/location, technical format, dimensionality, size, and basic quality metrics of the recorded readout. I excluded acquisition settings and instrument configuration because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded structure assignment or any interpreted results because those belong to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. No already_generated fields were provided in this turn, so there was no duplication constraint beyond staying within raw-signal territory.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw NMR data file as stored immediately after acquisition or export; use the exact filename string, e.g. 'sample123.fid' or 'sample123.dx'.
Digital file format of the raw NMR spectrum, recorded for the stored artefact; indicates how the signal is encoded for downstream processing.
Size of the raw NMR signal file in bytes, measured on storage after acquisition/export; typical range depends on experiment complexity and processing mode.
Number of dimensions in the raw NMR readout, recorded from the acquired artefact; indicates whether the spectrum is 1D, 2D, or higher-dimensional.
Number of sampled data points in each spectral dimension of the raw readout, recorded from the file contents; provide as a concise string such as '65536' for 1D or '1024x1024' for 2D.
Path, URI, or database location where the raw NMR file is stored, recorded after acquisition/export; use a stable string such as '/data/nmr/sample123.fid' or an accession URL.
Technical quality flag for the raw NMR readout, assessed on the stored signal before interpretation; indicates whether the artefact is usable for downstream processing.

mass_spectrometry.reasoning: I removed the three colliding instrument identity fields because they were already generated in earlier DAG steps and must not be repeated. I kept only mass-spectrometry-specific capture settings that describe the session configuration and not the instrument identity itself. I also retained fields that belong to the capture node rather than the resulting signal or downstream interpretation. No other already-generated overlaps were indicated, so the remaining fields avoid duplication while preserving the essential MS acquisition metadata.

md_schema.descr: Ionization mode selected for the mass spectrometry session, recorded at acquisition setup; indicates how molecules were converted to ions for measurement.
Mass analyzer type used during capture, recorded at setup; identifies the separation principle of the instrument used to record ion signals.
Acquired mass-to-charge range in m/z for the MS run, set before acquisition; provide the lower and upper bounds as a concise string such as '50-1500'.
Scan rate or acquisition speed used during the MS session, recorded at setup; use a numeric value representing scans per second when applicable, typically within the instrument's supported range.
Collision energy in electronvolts applied during the MS capture if tandem or fragmentation measurements were performed; typical range 0-200 eV.
Ion source temperature in degrees Celsius used during the MS session, controlled during acquisition; typical range 0-500 °C.

ms_spectrum.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw-data artefact properties of the MS spectrum: file identity, technical format, storage, dimensionality, and signal quality/peak-detection basics. I excluded capture settings such as manufacturer/model/serial, ionization mode, analyzer type, and acquisition parameters because those belong to the upstream Capture node. I also avoided any interpreted identity or mass assignment because those belong to downstream Process or Derivative nodes. Because earlier DAG steps already used several generic file/instrument-related field names, I chose distinct signal-focused names and avoided the colliding instrument fields called out by the user.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw mass spectrometry data file as stored immediately after acquisition or export; use the exact filename string, e.g. 'sample123.raw' or 'sample123.mzML'.
Digital file format of the raw MS spectrum, recorded for the stored artefact; indicates how the signal is encoded for downstream processing.
Size of the raw MS signal file in bytes, measured on storage after acquisition/export; typical range depends on scan count and export format.
Number of dimensions in the raw MS readout, recorded from the acquired artefact; indicates whether the dataset is 1D survey MS, MS/MS, or higher-dimensional if applicable.
Observed mass-to-charge range represented in the raw MS file, recorded from the stored artefact; provide a concise string such as '50-1500'.
Path, URI, or database location where the raw MS file is stored, recorded after acquisition/export; use a stable string such as '/data/ms/sample123.mzML' or an accession URL.
Technical quality flag for the raw MS readout, assessed on the stored signal before interpretation; indicates whether the artefact is usable for downstream processing.

nmr_structure_call.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only computational interpretation metadata: which algorithm or software performed the structure call, key analysis settings, confidence/quality of the assignment, and the outcome of the interpreted call. I excluded raw NMR file properties and acquisition settings because those belong to the Signal and Capture nodes, and I excluded the resulting structured identity itself because that belongs on the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided generic instrument fields that collided with earlier DAG steps and instead focused on process-specific software and interpretation parameters.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis package used to interpret the NMR spectrum and perform the structure call, recorded at the time of computation; e.g. 'MestReNova', 'ACD/Labs', or an in-house tool.
Version of the software used for the NMR interpretation step, recorded with the analysis run to support reproducibility; use a version string such as '14.2.1'.
Repository, package registry, or code source for the NMR analysis tool, recorded for reproducibility; provide a URL, package identifier, or internal repository string.

Reference library, database, or internal standard set used to support the NMR structure call, recorded at analysis time; provide a concise string such as 'in-house herbicide library' or a database name.
Algorithmic approach used to compare the experimental NMR spectrum to reference patterns, recorded during the interpretation step; describe the matching strategy in a concise controlled string.

Numerical confidence score for the NMR structure call, produced at the end of the interpretation process; typical range 0.0-1.0 or 0-100 depending on software, and should be stored consistently within the study.
Outcome status of the NMR interpretation step, recorded after review of the spectrum; indicates whether the structure call was accepted, tentative, rejected, or unresolved.

Concise description of the main structural motifs or substructures inferred from the NMR spectrum during interpretation, recorded as the process output summary; do not include full derived identity fields here.

ms_identity_call.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only computational interpretation metadata for the MS identity call: software provenance, analysis method, mass-calculation settings, and a confidence/outcome summary. I excluded raw mass-spectrum file properties and capture settings because those belong to the Signal and Capture nodes, and I excluded the final assigned identity itself because that belongs on the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided the previously colliding generic instrument fields and kept the schema process-specific and reproducible.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis package used to interpret the mass spectrum and support identity assignment, recorded at the time of computation; e.g. 'Xcalibur', 'MZmine', 'MassLynx', or an in-house tool.
Version of the software used for the MS interpretation step, recorded with the analysis run to support reproducibility; use a version string such as '3.5.0'.
Repository, package registry, or code source for the MS analysis tool, recorded for reproducibility; provide a URL, package identifier, or internal repository string.
Method used to infer molecular mass and identity from the spectrum, recorded during the interpretation step; describes the computational strategy used for peak matching and adduct handling.
Estimated monoisotopic mass in daltons produced by the MS identity call, recorded at the end of the analysis; typical range depends on compound size, often 100-2000 Da for small molecules.
Mass measurement or assignment error in parts per million for the identity call, calculated from observed versus expected mass; typical range approximately -100 to 100 ppm.

Numerical confidence score for the mass-spectrum-based identity assignment, produced at the end of the interpretation process; typical range 0.0-1.0 or 0-100 depending on software, and should be stored consistently within the study.
Outcome status of the MS interpretation step, recorded after review of the spectrum; indicates whether the identity assignment was accepted, tentative, rejected, or unresolved.

characterization_summary.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed summary outputs that integrate upstream NMR and MS interpretation: the consolidated identity result, summary confidence, physicochemical characterization summary, and a brief QC/usefulness indicator. I excluded raw signal properties, capture settings, and process software settings because those belong to the upstream Signal, Capture, and Process nodes. I also avoided duplicating batch/library identifiers already established earlier in the DAG and kept the fields focused on the synthesized characterization result itself.

md_schema.descr: Final interpreted compound name or assigned identity from the integrated characterization summary, produced after combining NMR and MS evidence; use the compound's accepted name or internal identifier string.

Overall status of the molecular identity assignment in the integrated characterization summary, recorded after review of NMR and MS evidence; indicates whether the identity was confirmed, tentative, or rejected.

Numerical confidence score for the integrated molecular identity and characterization summary, computed from the upstream interpretation outputs; typical range 0.0-1.0 or 0-100 depending on the analysis pipeline.

Concise summary of key physicochemical properties inferred or compiled in the characterization summary, such as mass, polarity, and major structural class; provide as a string because the exact set of properties may vary by compound.
High-level structural class assigned in the integrated summary, derived from combined NMR and MS evidence; use a controlled category describing the main chemical class.

Quality-control flag for the integrated characterization summary, indicating whether the combined evidence was sufficient for downstream bioassay use; assess after integration of the upstream interpretation results.

bioassay_setup.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only how the assay-ready treatments were prepared from characterized compounds: preparation format, dilution/solvent details, target panel selection, plate/setup parameters, and process-level readiness outcome. I excluded compound identity and characterization results because those belong to upstream Entity/Derivative nodes, and I excluded measurement capture settings and raw readouts because those belong to the downstream Capture/Signal nodes. No already_generated fields were provided here, so there was no duplication constraint beyond keeping the schema in the bioassay-preparation process layer.

md_schema.descr: Type of bioassay preparation performed for the compounds, recorded at setup; indicates the general biological testing format used for the downstream assay system.
Concise description of the plant enzyme or cellular pathway panel selected for testing, recorded when the assay is set up; include the biological targets or pathway classes in a short string.

Form in which the characterized compounds were prepared for assay readiness, recorded during setup; describes whether compounds were supplied as stocks, dilutions, pre-spotted plates, or other treatment formats.
Primary solvent or vehicle used to prepare assay-ready compound treatments, recorded at setup; provide the solvent name or mixture, e.g. 'DMSO' or 'ethanol:water'.
Final concentration in micromolar of each compound treatment prepared for the assay, set during bioassay preparation; typical range 0.001-1000 µM.
Well plate format used for the assay-ready treatment preparation, recorded at setup; indicates the physical format into which compounds were dispensed.
Number of technical or biological replicates prepared for each treatment condition, counted at assay setup; typical range 1-20.
Process-level status indicating whether the treated assay system was successfully prepared and ready for downstream capture, recorded after setup and quality checks.

treated_assay_system.reasoning: This is an Entity node, so I included only intrinsic properties of the exposed assay system after treatment: the biological target/context, organism and tissue/cell origin, exposure state, and any basic provenance needed to identify what the system is. I excluded preparation protocol details because those belong to the upstream bioassay setup Process, and I excluded instrument/capture settings and raw readouts because those belong to downstream Capture and Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating compound identity or potency metrics, since the treated system is the assay subject rather than the analysis result.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the treated assay system, assigned when the in vitro system is created and exposed to herbicide candidate compounds; use a stable string such as TAS-001.
Type of in vitro plant assay system represented by this entity at the time of treatment; indicates whether the system is an enzyme assay, cell-based assay, or mixed pathway system.
Plant species or cultivar from which the enzyme preparation, cells, or tissue used in the assay system was derived; record as a scientific name or cultivar string such as 'Arabidopsis thaliana'.
Primary plant enzyme or cellular pathway represented by the treated assay system at the point of exposure; provide a concise name such as 'acetolactate synthase' or 'auxin signaling'.
Current treatment state of the assay system, recorded after compounds have been added and before readout; describes whether the system is untreated, vehicle-treated, compound-treated, or control.
Duration in hours that the assay system has been exposed to the herbicide candidate compounds before measurement, recorded from treatment start to capture time; typical range 0.1-168 hours.
Estimated baseline viability or activity of the assay system immediately before treatment, measured at entity registration when available; typical range 0-100%.

bioactivity_assay_capture.reasoning: This is a Capture node, so I included only measurement-session and instrument-configuration metadata for the bioactivity assay capture: reader/instrument identity, detection mode, plate and timing settings, and acquisition parameters actively configured for the response measurement. I excluded treated-system properties and assay preparation details because those belong to the upstream Entity and Process nodes, and I excluded raw readout file properties because those belong to the downstream Signal node. I also avoided the already-colliding generic instrument fields by using assay-specific capture names that do not duplicate earlier steps.

md_schema.descr: Name or class of the assay instrument used for the bioactivity measurement session, recorded at acquisition setup; e.g. 'plate reader', 'fluorescence imager', or 'luminometer'.
Model name or number of the assay instrument used for the measurement session, recorded at acquisition setup; e.g. a specific reader or imaging system model.
Serial number of the assay instrument used for the capture session, recorded to identify the exact instrument configuration; use the manufacturer-assigned serial string.
Detection mode selected for the bioactivity assay capture, recorded at setup; indicates the physical readout principle used to measure response signals.
Excitation or emission wavelength in nanometers used for the assay measurement when applicable, set before acquisition; typical range 200-1000 nm.
Per-read integration time in milliseconds used by the assay instrument during capture, configured before acquisition; typical range 1-10000 ms.
Assay plate or vessel type used during the capture session, recorded at setup; describes the physical container holding the treated biological system.
Time in hours from the start of treatment to the bioactivity measurement session, recorded at capture; typical range 0.1-168 hours.
Detector gain or analogous sensitivity setting used for the bioactivity capture, configured at acquisition; used to optimize signal intensity and dynamic range.

bioactivity_signal.reasoning: This is a Signal node, so I included only raw assay-artefact properties: file identity/location, export format, dimensionality, basic content/size descriptors, and technical quality flags. I excluded capture instrument settings and measurement timing because those belong to the upstream Capture node, and I excluded potency/toxicity interpretation because that belongs to downstream Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided any fields that would collide with previously generated generic instrument names by keeping the schema focused on raw bioactivity data artefacts only.

md_schema.descr: Name of the raw bioactivity assay data file as stored immediately after acquisition or export; use the exact filename string, e.g. 'assay001.csv' or 'assay001.gpr'.
Digital file format of the raw assay readout, recorded for the stored artefact; indicates how the response signal is encoded for downstream processing.
Size of the raw bioactivity signal file in bytes, measured on storage after acquisition/export; typical range depends on plate size and export format.
Type of raw assay signal contained in the file, recorded from the artefact; indicates whether the readout is absorbance, fluorescence, luminescence, or another response signal.
Dimensions of the raw assay matrix or table, recorded from the stored file contents; provide as a concise string such as '96x8' or '384x1'.
Path, URI, or database location where the raw bioactivity file is stored, recorded after acquisition/export; use a stable string such as '/data/assays/assay001.csv' or an accession URL.
Technical quality flag for the raw assay readout, assessed on the stored signal before interpretation; indicates whether the artefact is usable for downstream processing.

potency_toxicity_quant.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only computational analysis metadata: software provenance, analysis method, fitting/model parameters, and the quantitative outputs that define the conversion from raw bioactivity readouts to potency, selectivity, and toxicity metrics. I excluded raw assay file properties, capture settings, and treated-system characteristics because those belong to Signal, Capture, and Entity nodes. I also avoided duplicating downstream summary fields by keeping the schema at the level of the quantification process rather than the final derivative report.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis package used to convert assay readouts into potency, selectivity, and toxicity metrics, recorded at the time of computation; e.g. 'GraphPad Prism', 'R', 'Python pipeline', or an in-house tool.
Version of the software used for the bioactivity quantification step, recorded with the analysis run to support reproducibility; use a version string such as '1.0.3'.
Repository, package registry, or code source for the bioactivity analysis tool, recorded for reproducibility; provide a URL, package identifier, or internal repository string.
Method used to normalize raw assay readouts before fitting potency or toxicity metrics, recorded during the quantification step; describes how response values were scaled or baseline-corrected.
Model used to fit concentration-response or response-response relationships during potency and toxicity quantification, recorded at analysis time; choose the fitting family applied to the assay data.
Primary potency metric computed from the assay readouts, recorded at the end of the analysis; examples include IC50, EC50, or inhibition percentage at a fixed concentration.

Numerical potency estimate produced by the bioactivity quantification step, recorded at the end of the analysis; units depend on the metric name, commonly nM or µM, with typical small-molecule ranges spanning 0.001-1000.
Computed selectivity index comparing target and off-target responses, recorded after analysis; typically a dimensionless ratio greater than or equal to 0.
Computed toxicity-related output from the assay analysis, recorded at the end of quantification; describes whether the compound shows evidence of adverse or nonspecific effects in the treated system.
Outcome status of the potency/toxicity quantification step, recorded after fitting and review; indicates whether the analysis was accepted, tentative, rejected, or unresolved.

bioactivity_metrics.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only computed summary outputs that aggregate the potency, selectivity, and toxicity results across targets and pathways: the final summary labels, key metric values, cross-target coverage, and an overall interpretation flag. I excluded raw assay readout properties, capture settings, and analysis software parameters because those belong to Signal, Capture, and Process nodes. I also avoided duplicating the upstream quantification process fields by focusing on the derived, reusable summary rather than the fitting workflow itself.

md_schema.descr: Derived potency class for the herbicide candidate, computed from the quantified bioactivity metrics after integrating across targets; use a consistent category reflecting the study's potency thresholds.

Best or representative potency value across the tested target panel, derived from the quantification step; units depend on the underlying metric, commonly nM or µM, and should be reported consistently within the dataset.
Derived selectivity classification for the herbicide candidate across targets and pathways, computed from the selectivity index and cross-target comparison.
Numeric selectivity score summarizing relative activity across targets or pathways, computed from the quantified bioactivity outputs; typically a dimensionless ratio or normalized score.
Derived classification of potential toxicity based on the assay metrics and cross-target response pattern, computed after integration of the bioactivity results.
Number of distinct enzyme or pathway targets used in the derivation of the summary metrics, counted after integrating the quantified assay results; typical range 1-100+.

Concise textual summary of the pathway-level bioactivity pattern inferred from the derived metrics, such as dominant efficacy, off-target activity, or generalized toxicity; keep as a string because the content may vary by compound.
Overall status of the derived bioactivity summary, indicating whether the aggregated metrics were accepted for downstream evaluation, flagged for review, or could not be determined.

joint_efficacy_analysis.reasoning: This is a Process node, so I included only the integrative analysis metadata: which upstream derivatives were combined, the evaluation framework, decision criteria, and the software/provenance for the joint assessment. I excluded raw signal and capture details because those belong to earlier Signal/Capture nodes, and I excluded the final report-style conclusions because those belong to the downstream Derivative node. I also avoided fields that would duplicate earlier characterization or bioactivity summary outputs, keeping this node focused on the integration procedure itself.

md_schema.descr: Name of the software or analysis package used to integrate characterization and bioactivity derivatives for the joint efficacy assessment, recorded at the time of computation; e.g. 'R', 'Python pipeline', or an in-house decision-support tool.
Version of the software used for the joint analysis step, recorded with the analysis run to support reproducibility; use a version string such as '2.1.0'.
Repository, package registry, or code source for the joint analysis tool, recorded for reproducibility; provide a URL, package identifier, or internal repository string.
Names of the upstream derivative inputs combined in this joint assessment, recorded at analysis time; should identify the characterization and bioactivity summary sources used in the integration.

Framework or decision rubric used to judge candidate suitability for agricultural application, recorded during the joint analysis; describes how identity, potency, selectivity, and toxicity were weighed.
Numeric threshold or cutoff used by the joint analysis to classify candidate suitability, recorded at setup; interpret in the units of the chosen scoring framework, typically dimensionless or 0-1.

Composite score produced by the joint analysis that summarizes overall candidate suitability for agricultural application, computed from the integrated derivatives; typical range depends on the framework and should be used consistently within the study.

Outcome status of the integrative analysis step, recorded after combination of characterization and bioactivity results; indicates whether the candidate passed, needs review, failed, or remained unresolved.

herbicide_evaluation_report.reasoning: This is a Derivative node, so I included only the final synthesized evaluation outputs: the overall candidate verdict, integrated summary fields, final ranking/score, and a concise applicability conclusion. I excluded upstream characterization, bioactivity, and joint-analysis process details because those belong to the earlier Process and Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating sample, batch, or instrument identifiers, since this node represents the final report-level assessment rather than provenance or acquisition metadata.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the final herbicide evaluation report, assigned when the derived assessment is created; use a stable string such as HERB-EVAL-001.

Overall final status assigned to the herbicide candidate in the evaluation report, recorded after integrating identity, potency, selectivity, and toxicity evidence; indicates whether the candidate is recommended, conditional, or not recommended for further agricultural development.

Composite final score summarizing herbicide candidate suitability for agricultural application, derived from the full workflow; typical range depends on the scoring framework and should be used consistently within the dataset.
Concise final summary of the confirmed molecular identity from the evaluation report, integrating NMR and MS characterization outcomes; provide the accepted compound name or brief identity statement.

Concise final summary of potency, selectivity, and potential toxicity from the evaluation report, integrating the bioactivity metrics across targets and pathways; provide as a string because the exact content may vary by candidate.
Relative priority rank of the candidate within the evaluated set, assigned in the final report to support downstream selection; use 1 as highest priority and larger integers for lower priority.
Brief narrative conclusion from the final evaluation report describing why the candidate was recommended or deprioritized, recorded as the final derivative output; keep as a compact string summary.
Overall status of the final evaluation report, indicating whether the report was completed and accepted for downstream decision-making or requires further review.
